extracted.intended_audience: general public / readers of entertainment and LGBT-related news
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and expectations for a stand-up comedian responding to harm caused by onstage remarks, including public apologies, reparative actions, and engagement with affected communities and advocacy groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use comedy to hurt anyone
rubrics_metrics.description: "I never want to use my comedy to hurt anyone."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article presents this explicit principle as part of Tracy Morgan's apology: comedic material should not inflict harm on individuals or groups. Use of this line in an apology signals recognition that comedy can cause real harm and that the performer should avoid harmful content going forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid promoting violence or advocating harm in jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid statements that endorse violence or harming others (e.g., the reported remark that he would 'pull out a knife and stab' his son and advice that bullied kids 'should just bust some ass').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece highlights these comments as examples of anti-patterns: language that suggests physical harm or revenge is inappropriate for comedic performance and likely to be received as hateful rather than humorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure offensive material is clearly framed as comedy (and not a rant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that reads like a rant rather than a joke (the blog: 'none of this rant was a joke') is more likely to be harmful and unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedians should craft material so that intent and comedic framing are clear; unframed hateful or hostile monologues will be interpreted as genuine animus and can cause serious harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: When harm occurs, issue timely apologies (written and verbal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow up hurtful remarks with an apology — Morgan released a written apology and also called GLAAD staffers by phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple modes of apology (written statement plus personal outreach) are recommended to acknowledge harm, show accountability, and open dialogue with affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver face-to-face apologies to directly affected audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Make personal, in-person apologies to those who were present and offended (Morgan agreed to return to Nashville to apologize in person to audience members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Face-to-face apologies demonstrate sincerity and allow for direct engagement and listening; working with local groups or event organizers can help facilitate these meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage and cooperate with advocacy groups for reparative action
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with relevant organizations (e.g., Morgan agreed to work with GLAAD and the Tennessee Equality Project and to record a PSA for GLAAD's campaign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnering with affected-community organizations helps shape meaningful reparative steps, such as public service announcements, anti-bullying campaigns, and meetings with affected individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include concrete reparative actions in response plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to specific actions beyond apologies — e.g., recording PSAs, meeting marginalized teens, supporting anti-bullying initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete commitments (campaign participation, meetings with victims, public messaging) signal accountability and contribute to restoration of trust more than words alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express support for equal rights and non-discrimination in apologies
rubrics_metrics.description: "Gay people deserve the same right to be happy in this country as everyone else."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An apology that explicitly affirms the rights and dignity of the harmed group reinforces the corrective message and clarifies the performer's stance against discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge personal context without excusing harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Situate remarks/apology within personal history (Morgan referenced being bullied, his brother's disability, and his father's death from AIDS) while not using context to excuse harmful statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing personal background can explain perspectives or growth, but should not be presented as justification for offensive conduct; it is better used to explain how harm was caused and how the performer will change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue corrective messaging proactively before further appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver the revised message in other venues prior to additional performances (Morgan planned to deliver his new message in New York before going to Nashville).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive corrective statements at upcoming appearances help control the narrative, show learning, and reduce the chance of repeating harm.
